title: Resurrection Mary: The Ghost Who Asks for a Ride on Archer Avenue

sources.what: 'a young, fashionable blonde woman'; linked to the Oh Henry Ballroom (later Willowbrook) in Willow Springs; no answer conclusive
first sighting 1939 (Jerry Palus); the August 1976 bent gate bars; drivers who said they hit her (1989); no conclusive record
she 'vanishes when they arrive at Resurrection Cemetery'
'a young blond woman in a white ballgown who requests a ride somewhere along Archer Avenue'
Aug. 10, 1976: Patrolman found the gate bars pulled apart; a worker said a truck backed into the gate (1992 Chicago Tribune); drivers say the car cut through her
the legend; 1996 driver 'couldn't find the body'; the bars bent by a crew member's truck
Resurrection Cemetery, consecrated 1904, 7201 Archer Road, Justice

beats.text: She asks you for a ride home. Then, at the cemetery gates, she's gone.
beats.label: ARCHER AVENUE, ILLINOIS

beats.text: On Archer Avenue, southwest of Chicago, drivers have told this story since the 1930s.
beats.label: SINCE THE 1930s
beats.credit: WBEZ; CBS Chicago; Ghost Research Society

beats.text: Legend says she's a young blond woman, dressed for dancing, near the old Oh Henry Ballroom.
beats.label: THE OH HENRY BALLROOM
beats.credit: Chicago History Museum; Hinsdale Magazine; Ursula Bielski

beats.text: She asks for a ride up Archer. When the car reaches Resurrection Cemetery, the seat is empty.
beats.label: RESURRECTION CEMETERY

beats.text: Some drivers say they hit a woman on Archer. When they stopped, no one was there.
beats.label: WHAT DRIVERS SAY
beats.credit: CBS Chicago; Ghost Research Society; Ursula Bielski

beats.text: In August 1976, a police officer found two bars of the cemetery gate bent and scorched. A worker later said a truck had backed into it.
beats.label: AUGUST 1976
beats.credit: CBS Chicago; Ghost Research Society; Ursula Bielski

beats.text: Who was she? No one has ever proven it. But the legend says she's still waiting for a ride.
beats.label: STILL WAITING

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: Lines 1, 3-5 supported as legend. 'Late 1930s' became 'the 1930s'; 1976 bars 'bent and scorched' added; 'still out there' became 'the legend says she's still waiting'; small-town ballroom drawing replaced.
